items: Hear an exercise's setup read aloud, part by part from your feet up to your grip and breathing: tap "Read the setup aloud" in the Brief tab, or in any Body Position table. Exercises without their own table get the setup for their movement pattern.
AI cowork replies now wait for you to review them before they change your log. Tick what to keep, discard the rest, and undo anything applied. Switch review off per channel in Settings → Cowork.
The app now starts in light or dark to match your device, until you pick a theme. Settings → Theme → Match device goes back to following it.
Settings → Data → Erase all GymTracker data now really clears everything this app keeps on the device. It always asks first, and your Google Drive copy is never touched.
New default font, Atkinson Hyperlegible, built for easy reading. Settings → Font switches to System, Serif or Monospace.
Exercise animations are clearer and anatomically right, and about 50 new movements have their own figure: sit-ups, L-sits, seated rows, thrusters, burpees, sled work, mace and club swings and more.
A workout that runs past midnight stays live, and its timers keep going.
On a computer, the app uses more of the screen, up to a comfortable width.

Added the five Freemotion Row movements, the seated low-row machine, the swing to lunge high pull, the half-kneeling blind-spot rotation, the Spartan uppercut and the partner-held floor back extension.
End Workout now takes a single tap.
Record or upload your own sound, up to 5 seconds, for a PR, a progress set, the end of a rest or the end of a workout.
With a heart-rate monitor connected, you get an estimate of calories burned.
Coach's choice: on a plan step, the coach picks the best of the filtered options for you.
The next-set card also shows the S-rank set when it is within reach.
Starting a plan offers a 1.5× volume option, and can pick the volume for you from the time you want to finish by.
More timed holds in the exercise list.

Next-set coach: a challenging but achievable target for your next set, from your history, sets so far, rest, heart rate and what is left in the plan. It sticks to weights you have used and works around one you type.
Recovery data from any wearable (sleep, HRV, resting heart rate and more) is trended and can steer the next set. You can switch any factor off.
A live grade for the current exercise, and a grade trend line across the workout at the end.
Your gym chain's locations can be filled in for you, with your gym usage history and a heat map.
An option to try pairing your heart-rate monitor whenever a workout starts.
